The context pass changed the diagnosis in one load-bearing way: the absolute
floor **already existed in #2221 and was computed, recorded, and then consumed
by nothing.** This is a wire-up + surface gap, not a missing-constant gap.

**Context resolved from project knowledge:**

- **Near-duplicate scan: none.** `tasks/*/*/body.md` grep for
  `trainability floor|per-cell (realized )?yield|yield.shortfall` matches only
  the parent #2221 and this task. No prior issue or rule covers an absolute
  per-cell row floor.

- **#2221 already had the constant.** `MIX_MIN_ROWS_PER_CELL = 32`
  (`src/explore_persona_space/experiments/issue_2221/constants.py:143`) is
  evaluated at `scripts/issue2221_build_mix.py:179`
  (`below = len(mix_rows) < C.MIX_MIN_ROWS_PER_CELL`) and written into the P3
  manifest as `below_floor` + `min_rows_floor`. Grep for consumers of that
  flag: **zero** — `issue2221_finetune_sweep.py` has no row-count gate of any
  kind (its only asserts are family/version membership and adapter presence).
  The evil cell was flagged `below_floor: true` at 1 row and fine-tuned,
  captured, and judged anyway. Positive precedent that DOES act on the same
  flag: `scripts/issue2054_phase_a.py:1530-1535`.

- **The fail-loud gate pattern already exists — on the OTHER data path.**
  `src/explore_persona_space/artifacts/datagen.py` computes
  `floor_n = ceil(quota_floor * target_n)` (default `quota_floor=0.8`, L1349/1446)
  and raises `DatagenYieldError` at the row-counting site when
  `len(pos_kept) < floor_n` (L1547-1556; class docstring L127: "loud, names
  yields"). So proposed-change item 2 is a *reuse-and-generalize*, not a new
  mechanism: the gate must become callable from a real-corpus judge-banded mix
  builder like #2221's, which never touches `datagen.py`.

- **The existing floor is RELATIVE, which is the actual hole.**
  `.claude/rules/on-policy-completions.md` (pre-registered-quota block) already
  carries DROP semantics — "a source below the floor is DROPPED ... and the drop
  is REPORTED as a finding" — plus the >=90% close-miss single escalation tranche
  and equalize-down to floor-N. But every floor there is a *fraction of target*.
  Nothing anywhere pins an **absolute** minimum, so equalize-down to
  `min(non-empty versions)` can legally land at 1 row and still pass every gate.

- **Body correction to carry into the plan:** the body attributes the
  "REPORTED / DROPPED" language to both `on-policy-completions.md` **and**
  `data-realism.md`. Grep of `data-realism.md` for
  `floor|yield|drop|below|insufficient|too few|not enough`: **zero hits**. That
  rule is tier-preference only; the plan must not cite it as an anchor.

- **Grounding anchor for the default constant (item 1's "not invented"):**
  install evidence in `.claude/rules/marker-training-recipe.md` is denominated
  in **optimizer steps**, not rows — narrowest observed install transition
  ~12 steps, 30-step all-arm anchor (#533/#547), steps dominate LoRA rank
  (#546). So an absolute row floor is derivable
  (`rows >= steps_floor x effective_batch / epochs`) rather than asserted, and
  #2221's own 32 is testable against it (32 rows @ 1 epoch is ~4 optimizer steps
  at batch 8 — below the ~12-step transition, i.e. 32 may itself be too low).
  Prior-issue floor precedents: #906/#1090 (sycophancy 6/36 vs floor 20).
  That rule also supplies the placement precedent for item 2 —
  "Training-row token budget (the #260 sibling — **gate at mix BUILD time**)".

- **Item 3's review surface already exists and pushes the OPPOSITE way.**
  `critic-lens-reference.md` item 9(i) REVISEs plans that gate inclusion on a
  continuous quantity with "no graceful-degradation floor", citing #612 (a
  source at 194/200 discarded wholesale). The new rule must be written as an
  explicit **two-tier** contract — absolute *trainability* floor => DROP
  (below it the cell is not a condition at all), relative *target* floor =>
  equalize-down / keep — or it will collide with lens 9(i) head-on. Plan must
  state the reconciliation, not just add a third gate.

**Assumption (autonomous, stated per auto-continuation policy):** the fix
EXTENDS `.claude/rules/on-policy-completions.md` + the existing
`artifacts/datagen.py` floor gate rather than adding a new `.claude/rules/*.md`
file, per the task body's own scope note ("prefer extending the existing
yield/band-count machinery over adding a parallel gate"). No `LESSONS.md` index
row is added.

Gap = absolute floor + wire-up + two-tier reconciliation with critic lens 9(i).

`consistency-checker` verifies that a new EXPERIMENT plan changes only one
variable from its parent experiment and uses matching baselines, eval suites,
seeds, and data versions — including the reused-artifact inheritance case.

#2242 is `kind: infra`: a 0-GPU-h workflow-surface + library fix. It registers
no conditions, no seeds, no eval suite, no DV, no baseline, and reuses no
trained artifact. Its `parent_id: 2221` records the INCIDENT SOURCE (the run
whose 1-row cell exposed the gap), not a recipe ancestor whose hyperparameters
this plan inherits — so there is no parent recipe to diff against and every
check the agent owns evaluates vacuously. The #1732 no-parent skip branch does
not apply here (a parent IS set); this skip is on kind-and-substance grounds.

The single-variable question this plan DOES raise — whether the absolute floor
collides with the relative equalize-down floor already in
`.claude/rules/on-policy-completions.md`, and with `critic-lens-reference.md`
item 9(i) which pushes the opposite way — is a CONTRACT-coherence question, not
a parent-recipe-inheritance question. It was routed to the Claude `critic`
under the Methodology lens instead, which returned REVISE on exactly that axis
(the item-9 N/A escape lets the #2221 shape self-exempt from the new DROP
direction). That finding is being folded in plan v5.
